newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re U.S. cool on Credit Suisse talk.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re U.S. cool on Credit Suisse talk.

text.p: The head of Swiss Reinsurance Co 's U.S. operations dismissed rumours that the reinsurer could merge with Credit Suisse Group, saying this would endanger Swiss Re's efforts to diversify.

"Everyone thinks it has to happen that Swiss Re and Credit Suisse merge. I don't see this as inevitable at all," Swiss Reinsurance America Corp chairman Heidi Hutter told reporters at the St. Gallen Management Symposium.

"In fact from the standpoint of a reinsurer, our great strength is our diversity...by geography and product line. For that and to maintain that, we are very careful not to ever have an exclusive distribution channel," she added.
"I can't see enough strength out of the unification that would overcome the potential loss of diversity."
Rumours that the two companies could extend their close links into a formal merger have swelled occasionally on financial markets, but neither company has said it was envisioning such a step.
On other subjects, Hutter said Swiss Re's U.S. operations were doing well so far this year, but it was taking care not to venture into overly risky areas.
"It is a very competitive market and that is why we have said all along that we are working on the quality and will focus on bottom line, not top line," she said

"We are working on the fundamentals," she said, noting first-quarter 1997 results, as reported along statutory U.S. lines, had improved over the year-earlier period's. First quarter net income was $75 million in the U.S., compared with $191.6 million for all of 1996, she said.
"If we wanted to chase volume it would be very easy to grow the volume of the businesses but it would have bad consequences now and in the future for the result," she said.
